acceptance_screen.note: local synthetic screening limits, not production SLOs; the unoptimized merged control is expected to expose index regressions

environment.benchmark_filesystem: /tmp on tmpfs; persistent-disk I/O is not represented

index_profiles.dual_legacy_index: separate user.db/media.db with single-column recognition indexes and a server/title media index
index_profiles.merged_legacy_index: one nastools.db with the same legacy index profile
index_profiles.merged_optimized: one nastools.db with composite recognition and generation-aware media indexes

methodology.cold_read: best-effort POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED request; not guaranteed to evict page cache
methodology.full_sync_overlap: 15 seconds per profile; 50,000 media rows; 5,000 history rows; media batch interval 0 (saturated); reader 10 ms, history write 100 ms, subscription update 500 ms, cleanup 500 ms
methodology.layout_order: dual legacy indexes, merged legacy indexes, then optimized merged indexes
limitations: synthetic rows and direct sqlite3 connections; does not exercise SQLAlchemy application pool
subscription and media source behavior are simulated locally; no real media server or 12-hour schedule
tmpfs benchmark storage does not represent persistent-disk latency or durability behavior
runs were sequential single samples, not statistically repeated production acceptance
methodology.steady_state_runs: 5 seconds per layout with 4 readers; batch size 500; 8 KiB recognition payload; same seeded app-shaped rows

runs.cache_note: first-read timings use best-effort POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED; hot-read percentiles follow explicit warm-up
runs.load_note: zero operation intervals offer saturated work; nonzero intervals control offered workload
runs.note: synthetic sqlite3 workload; dual/merged legacy-index profiles isolate merge effect; optimized merged profile adds composite indexes; not app pool, production data, or scheduled-sync acceptance
